nodes.label: Canonical Model Layer Stack
nodes.rationale: Documents the layer stack (Frontend -> Canonical Model -> Frappe Mapping -> Business Behaviour -> Relationships -> Workflow -> Stock/Accounting/Tax Impact -> API Behaviour -> Permissions -> ERPNext Source Reference -> Behavioral Tests -> Future Native Backend) that docs/backend/ follows, distinct from the deployment/runtime layered architecture in docs/architecture.md.

nodes.label: Two Backends, One Product
nodes.rationale: Frames Frappe/ERPNext as the current reference/operational backend (not the target architecture) while Ceylon Stack canonical models are the long-term product architecture, with the intent to progressively replace Frappe module by module without redesigning the frontend.

nodes.label: MFG-VAL-006 Quality Readiness rule
nodes.rationale: Quality Readiness must read Job Card's own quality_inspection_template/quality_inspection fields, never fall back to the production Item's own template default, since that would infer Work-Order-level readiness from an unrelated Item-level setting; deliberate design choice, distinct from mcp-server's own Item-level approach for a different purpose.

nodes.label: MFG-STK-001 fg_completed_qty gate
nodes.rationale: ERPNext's Stock Entry.update_work_order only calls add_additional_items()/update_work_order_qty() when fg_completed_qty is truthy; omitting it let a Stock Entry submit cleanly while silently never attaching the additional item to required_items. Fixed by threading preview.fg_completed_qty through the form and validating presence before submit.

nodes.label: MFG-STK-002 Additional material lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Submitting an extra non-BOM item line calls add_additional_items(), inserting a Work Order Item row with is_additional_item=1 and voucher_detail_reference, bypassing the update-after-submit block because it is a targeted server-side child-row insert, not doc.save(). Cancelling calls remove_additional_items().

nodes.label: MFG-STK-003 Quantity headroom
nodes.rationale: Total transferable qty per item is capped at required_qty * (1 + Manufacturing Settings.transfer_extra_materials_percentage/100), currently 0% on this instance; live-confirmed rejection of a 200-unit excess transfer.

nodes.label: MFG-VAL-004 Warehouse validity server-side
nodes.rationale: ERPNext independently rejects a group warehouse server-side even though the frontend's warehouse picker already filters to is_group=0, disabled=0.

nodes.label: MFG-WF-003 Draft never moves stock
nodes.rationale: Only Submit moves stock; a Draft Material Transfer for Manufacture Stock Entry leaves Bin.actual_qty and transferred_qty unchanged, so the frontend exposes saveTransferDraftAction and submitTransferAction as two separate actions rather than one implicit save-and-submit.

nodes.label: MFG-VAL-005 Batch/serial guard
nodes.rationale: Frontend-only safety: rows whose item has has_batch_no/has_serial_no are disabled in the form since no batch/serial picker UI exists yet; not an ERPNext-enforced block at this step.

nodes.label: MFG-VAL-001 Production Item create restriction
nodes.rationale: Frontend-only restriction: New Work Order only lists items with default_bom set, this app's own definition of 'manufacturable', not an ERPNext DocType constraint.

nodes.label: MFG-CALC-001 Required qty scaling
nodes.rationale: required_qty = bom_item.qty * (work_order.qty / bom.quantity), computed server-side by ERPNext on insert; the frontend's BOM preview only mirrors this for display, never sends it.

nodes.label: MFG-VAL-002 Update-after-submit block
nodes.rationale: Neither required_items nor any Work Order Item child field carries allow_on_submit:1, so Frappe's core _validate_update_after_submit() rejects any edit once docstatus=1; this is core Frappe safety, not a gap, with MFG-WF-002 as the real native path.

nodes.label: MFG-VAL-003 Draft-stage required_qty reversion
nodes.rationale: While allow_editing_of_items_and_quantities_in_work_order=0, every save calls set_required_items(reset_only_qty=True) which resets required_qty but never resets item_code, so a raw item substitution on a Draft row persists even though qty edits are silently reverted.

nodes.label: MFG-WF-001 Create-only lifecycle in this frontend
nodes.rationale: This frontend only ever calls createDoc, never submitDoc/cancelDoc on Work Order itself; every created Work Order stays at docstatus 0 (Draft) from this app's perspective.
nodes.norm_label: mfg-wf-001 create-only lifecycle in this frontend

nodes.label: MFG-WF-002 Stock-Entry-driven material deviation
nodes.rationale: The ERPNext-native mechanism for a Work-Order-specific material deviation is Stock-Entry-driven, not a Work Order edit — a deliberate Package 4 investigation outcome, not an assumption.

nodes.label: Default Operating Mode (single agent + small package)
nodes.rationale: Exists because unrestricted agent usage was observed to create high token cost, oversized sessions, weak review/QA ratio, scope creep, and architectural drift (100% subagent-heavy sessions, 55% >150k context, ~47% dominated by frontend-dev, low code-reviewer/qa-tester usage).
nodes.norm_label: default operating mode (single agent + small package)

nodes.label: Canonical Model, Not Frappe Coupling
nodes.rationale: Mandates documenting Frontend field -> Ceylon Stack canonical field -> Current Frappe mapping (never just Frontend->Frappe) so the canonical layer is Ceylon Stack's own business architecture, with Frappe as one current implementation, distinguishing REQUIRED_CEYLON_BEHAVIOR / FRAPPE_CURRENT_BEHAVIOR / FRAPPE_ONLY_IMPLEMENTATION_DETAIL.

nodes.label: Job Card Naming Series Correction (PO-JOB, not JC-.YYYY.-)
nodes.rationale: docs/mcp-agents-plan.md guessed a JC-.YYYY.- naming series for Job Card; the real live series confirmed via bench console is PO-JOB.#####, so anything built against the guessed format would break against real IDs.
